title: Back up button on the Mac dashboard writes the all-projects backup and shows it in Finder

requirements.text: The dashboard header has a Back up button that runs genlock backup --all
requirements.check: file: DashboardView.swift DashboardHeader has the button calling model.backupAll()

requirements.text: Clicking it writes an archive to ~/genlock-backups, reveals it in Finder, and says how many records it saved
requirements.check: eye: TJ clicks Back up on the dashboard and Finder shows the new genlock-all archive

requirements.text: The app builds and its tests pass with the button in
requirements.check: swift build and swift test in app/ exit 0

evidence: DashboardView.swift DashboardHeader: 'Back up' GlassButton (shown when there are projects, disabled while running) calls model.backupAll(), which runs genlock backup --all --json via GenlockCLI (timeout 120s)
app/: swift build -> Build complete (41s); swift test -> 158 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped

text: Button built and tested in the repo; not in the running app until TJ updates again. Req 2 is TJ's eye check: click Back up, Finder opens on ~/genlock-backups/genlock-all-*.tar.gz, banner says N records from M projects.
TJ clicked it: works (874 records, 6 projects). Banner trimmed to 'Backed up N records from M projects' at his ask; Finder already opens the folder with the file selected. Builds.

evidence: TJ clicked Back up in the updated app; banner read 'Backed up 874 records from 6 projects to ~/genlock-backups/genlock-all-20261113-062941.tar.gz'; asked if Finder opened, TJ: 'ok great'
